title: Audit result
description: The result of `houserules audit` for a range of commits: the rules of the package with one row each, the counts of the rows, and the verdict on the work-item references of the range.

base.description: The short sha of the commit that `--base` names.

head.description: The short sha of the commit that `--head` names, `HEAD` by default.

ids.description: The ids that `--ids` adds to the package, in the order given.

changed_files.description: The files that the range adds, copies, modifies, or renames, as paths from the install root, in the order of the diff.

areas.description: The areas that the changed files touch, sorted.

area_files.description: The changed files of each area. `global` comes first; every other area follows in the order in which a changed file first matches it.

rules.description: One row for each rule of the package, sorted by id.

stale_sanctions.description: One line for each `--sanctioned` booking on a deterministic row that did not fail. Absent when there is none.

references.description: The verdict on the work-item references of the range.

AuditRow.description: The row of one rule in an audit result.

id.description: The id of the knowledge entry.

mode.description: Whether the audit ran a check for the rule or leaves the rule to a reviewer.

level.description: The level of the check, or `null` for a judged row.

result.description: What the check found, or `open` for a judged row.

evidence.description: The line that names what the check found, or `—` for a judged row.

findings.description: The results of a `runner` check with a SARIF tool that count, in the order of the calls. Only the row of such a check holds the key.

sanctioned.description: The reference of the `--sanctioned` booking on the row. Only a judged row and a failed deterministic row hold the key.

RowMode.description: Whether the audit ran a check for a rule.

oneOf.description: The rule has a check, and the audit ran it.
The rule has no check; a reviewer judges it.

RowLevel.description: The level of a check: what a violation of the check counts as.

oneOf.description: A violation warns and fails nothing.
A check of level `fail` is violated.
A check of level `warn` is violated.
A judged row: a reviewer decides.

Finding.description: One result of a `runner` check that counts, as the row lists it.

path.description: The file, relative to the install root with `/` separators. A location outside the root keeps the fully resolved URI of its base when it has one, else the URI as the tool wrote it. `null` for a result with no location.

line.description: The line in `path`; `null` with no path or no region.

rule.description: The id of the rule, or `(no rule id)`.

message.description: The text of the message, or `(no message)`.

Summary.description: The counts of the rows of an audit result.

base.description: The short sha of the commit that `--base` names.

head.description: The short sha of the commit that `--head` names.

deterministic.description: The number of rows with the mode `deterministic`.

pass.description: The number of deterministic rows with the result `pass`.

fail.description: The number of deterministic rows with the result `fail`.

warn.description: The number of deterministic rows with the result `warn`.

skipped.description: The number of deterministic rows with the result `skipped`.

judged.description: The number of rows with the mode `judged`.

empty_range.description: `true` when the range holds no commit. Absent otherwise.

sanctioned_fail.description: The number of failed rows that hold `sanctioned`. Absent when there is none.

References.description: What the audit decided about the work-item references of the range: the `Work-Item:` and `Deferred:` trailers of its commits and the backlog ids of the deliverables it read.

checked.description: The number of references that the tracker judged, passed or failed.

passed.description: The number of references among those checked that passed.

skipped.description: The number of references that the audit did not judge: all of them when the install has no tracker, when the tracker cannot be reached, or when the tracker answered with an error.

failures.description: One line for each failure, in the order that the audit prints them on stderr.
